c277fd563613cda6767258838574386d16e830eb.summary: The Swiss government CERT (GovCERT) analysed Fobber, a new e-banking Trojan that appears to be a spinoff of Tinba, to check whether Swiss critical infrastructure was targeted. Highlights include function-level encryption that keeps code encrypted until it is called, position-independent code, and hash-based import resolution. The report says the samples it examined seem to share one campaign key. It knows of no Swiss financial institutions targeted so far.

c267080d9a999024efcf6e8080055569dd842f42.summary: DataBreaches reports that the AlphV ransomware group attacked Cadre Services, a Wisconsin employment and staffing firm, in 2023. AlphV claimed to have taken 100 GB of files and demanded $300,000. After talks stalled at a $35,000 offer, it leaked files containing personal and identity data. The report says some of its own claims could not be verified.

c2fe4faed629239ed3b7bd3c8f9f8ac0342f8e70.summary: SentinelOne reports a new variant of Operation In(ter)ception, a macOS campaign it links to the North-Korean linked Lazarus group (aka Nukesped). Lures use job vacancies at a rival cryptocurrency exchange, following a Coinbase-themed variant that ESET spotted in August 2022. The malware uses a persistence agent, a second-stage app and a downloader with hardcoded C2. The C2 was offline during analysis, so the final payload was not retrieved.
